segments: Two sets of templates to copy and use:
Configuration template (.sops.yaml): sops client encryption rules, specifying “which files are encrypted with which public keys”
Encryption template (host/sops.nix): the sops-nix NixOS module, specifying “what to decrypt at runtime, where to write it, and who can read it”

This article explains general-purpose templates checked against current upstream SOPS and sops-nix source code. The SOPS CLI version is not the sops-nix module version. Before deploying a project, still check the sops-nix revision pinned in flake.lock.

Read before use AGE_RECIPIENT_PLACEHOLDER_NOT_VALID in the templates is a placeholder. Before copying and using a template, replace it with your own real public key; otherwise, sops parsing will fail with malformed recipient. The same applies to sections marked with # 示例 comments.

Place it at the repository root. By default, the current SOPS CLI searches upward from the working directory for .sops.yaml; when invoking it across directories, specify --config explicitly. The target file path is matched against rules relative to the configuration directory. Rules are matched from top to bottom, and the first match wins, so put more specific rules first.
Match file paths (relative to the .sops.yaml directory)
age recipients; comma-separated string at the top level, array within key_groups
PGP fingerprints; comma-separated string at the top level, array within key_groups
AWS KMS ARNs; string at the top level, array of objects in key_groups
GCP KMS resource IDs; array of resource_id objects in key_groups
Key groups (one key per line allows comments)
Number of groups required for decryption
Encrypt keys ending with this suffix
Leave keys ending with this suffix in plaintext (default: _unencrypted)
One key / one file: a flat string such as age: "..." is simplest
Multiple keys with ownership comments: use key_groups + arrays, with a comment on each key's line
Multiple environments / teams: one rule per environment, specific rules first and fallback last
System-level configuration specifying the runtime “decryption source, output location, file ownership, and permissions.”
true = decrypt through a systemd service; the default also depends on options such as userborn
Generate if keyFile does not exist

Decryption sources can coexist age.keyFile and age.sshKeyPaths are not mutually exclusive, and age and GnuPG sources can also be declared together. Choosing sources is a permissions and maintenance decision; do not misrepresent mechanisms that can coexist as a type constraint. Key locations must be readable at the selected decryption stage, and private keys must never enter the Nix store.
Template three: sops-nix runtime configuration rendering

The first two templates are examples of CLI and module configuration, a different concept from actual sops.templates. The latter contains only placeholders during Nix evaluation; after secrets are decrypted, the installer substitutes the actual contents, keeping plaintext out of the store.

Templates normally output to /run/secrets/rendered/<name>; referring to them through .path is more robust. You can set content/file, path, owner/group, mode, and restartUnits/reloadUnits to run on changes. Placeholder replacement does not automatically escape JSON, YAML, shell syntax, or EnvironmentFile contents. If a secret contains newlines, quotes, or special characters, design around the consuming format. The example above requires values safely encoded for EnvironmentFile; for complex secrets, it is preferable for the application to read credential files directly. This is only a snippet, not a complete deployed service.
